def ref_attention(q, k, v):
    """Single-head attention: softmax(Q Kt / sqrt(d)) V, with q, k, v all [seq, dim].

    This level exists to show that the harness is not about matmul. It was added by writing this
    reference and one input builder -- nothing else in the file changed. Do the same for whatever you
    care about.

    Note the trap, which is the whole reason attention is interesting on a chip: a naive exp()
    overflows. The reference subtracts the row max first, and a kernel that does not will return
    plausible numbers on friendly data and NaN on real data.
    """
    d = q.shape[1]
    scores = (q.astype(np.float32) @ k.astype(np.float32).T) / np.sqrt(d)
    scores = scores - scores.max(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    e = np.exp(scores)
    return ((e / e.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)) @ v.astype(np.float32)).astype(q.dtype)

tensor_copy from psum into an sbuf tile, then dma_copy that out to the shared_hbm output.

import nki
import nki.isa as nisa
import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def nki_attention_(q, k, v):
    S, D = q.shape                            # S, D <= 128: every operand is ONE tile
    out = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=q.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    q_t = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=q.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    k_t = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=k.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    v_t = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=v.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=q_t, src=q)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=k_t, src=k)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=v_t, src=v)

    # Transpose q and k to (D, S) in SBUF
    qT_p = nl.ndarray((D, S), dtype=q.dtype, buffer=nl.psum)
    kT_p = nl.ndarray((D, S), dtype=k.dtype, buffer=nl.psum)
    nisa.nc_transpose(dst=qT_p, data=q_t)
    nisa.nc_transpose(dst=kT_p, data=k_t)
    qT = nl.ndarray((D, S), dtype=q.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    kT = nl.ndarray((D, S), dtype=k.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.tensor_copy(dst=qT, src=qT_p)
    nisa.tensor_copy(dst=kT, src=kT_p)

    # Compute scores (S, S) = q @ kT / sqrt(D)
    scores_p = nl.ndarray((S, S), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nisa.nc_matmul(dst=scores_p, stationary=q_t, moving=kT)
    nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=scores_p, data=1.0 / np.sqrt(D), op0=nl.multiply)

    # Subtract row max to avoid overflow
    max_p = nl.ndarray((S, 1), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nl.sum(view=scores_p, axis=[1], dst=max_p)
    nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=scores_p, data=max_p, op0=nl.subtract)

    # Compute exp(scores)
    scores_exp_p = nl.ndarray((S, S), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nisa.activation(op=nl.exp, dst=scores_exp_p, src=scores_p)

    # Compute softmax
    sum_exp_p = nl.ndarray((S, 1), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nl.sum(view=scores_exp_p, axis=[1], dst=sum_exp_p)
    nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=scores_exp_p, data=sum_exp_p, op0=nl.divide)

    # Transpose scores_exp to (S, S) for matmul with v
    scores_exp_t_p = nl.ndarray((S, S), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nisa.nc_transpose(dst=scores_exp_t_p, data=scores_exp_p)
    scores_exp_t = nl.ndarray((S, S), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.tensor_copy(dst=scores_exp_t, src=scores_exp_t_p)

    # Compute output (S, D) = scores_exp @ v
    o_p = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum)
    nisa.nc_matmul(dst=o_p, stationary=scores_exp_t, moving=v_t)
    o = nl.ndarray((S, D), dtype=q.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.tensor_copy(dst=o, src=o_p)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=out, src=o)
    return out
